points.problem: Enable mouse in STREAM_IO and disable QuickEdit
points.evidence: The historical P11/P12 notes conflict and are not sufficient necessity evidence. Current selected video.c enable_stream_io sets both common stream_io_enabled and host state. mouse_io_interrupt calls disable_stream_io before any INT33 dispatch; host_disable_stream_io enables WINDOW_INPUT and MOUSE_INPUT. Presentation-only startup disables StreamIoSwitchOn, so original SetupConsoleMode enables both flags itself. Thus unconditional MOUSE_INPUT is redundant. Modern QuickEdit remains a distinct native interception: console_client mode_client/GET_MODE/SET_MODE transport the actual frontend Console mode; console_frontend uses native GetConsoleMode/SetConsoleMode without normalization; no other selected owner clears QuickEdit. Restoring the complete original setup retains an initially enabled QuickEdit bit even after mouse activation, leaving Console selection enabled instead of exclusive guest mouse records. This is a source/API contract counterexample, not a newly observed physical click failure.
points.minimum: Restore original conditional mouse/window OR; retain one mode expression to set EXTENDED_FLAGS and clear QUICK_EDIT_MODE. No helper, new state or relocated policy.
